items.explanation: 百 is read ヒャク, but the sound changes after some numbers: 三百 (さんびゃく), 六百 (ろっぴゃく), 八百 (はっぴゃく).
items.mnemonic: 一 on top of 白 (white): one hundred white hairs.

items.explanation: 千 is read セン, and it changes to ぜん after three: 三千 (さんぜん). The kun reading ち appears in place names such as 千葉 (ちば).
items.mnemonic: 十 with a stroke on its head: ten counted many, many times.

items.explanation: Japanese counts big numbers in units of ten thousand, 万 (マン), not thousands: 100,000 is 十万 (じゅうまん, ten man).
items.mnemonic: A table with a hook under it, strong enough to hold ten thousand coins.
items.culture_note: 万 also means countless or all: 万歳 (ばんざい, banzai), the cheer, literally means ten thousand years.

items.explanation: 円 is the Japanese currency, read エン. English says yen, but in Japanese it is pronounced えん. It also means circle; the native reading appears in まるい (round).
items.mnemonic: A window with a coin standing inside it.
items.culture_note: A common explanation is that the name comes from the round shape of the coins. The yen became Japan's currency in 1871.
